stances.summary: Criticizes public apathy toward Ukraine war as historically dangerous
stances.quote: Frankly i’m getting tired of hearing people “losing interest” in the war in Ukraine like it’s a hobby or new toy.  History isn’t kind to those who don’t pay attention to world events or read the room, even when it’s uncomfortable, especially when it’s uncomfortable.

stances.summary: Frames NATO inaction against Russian convoy as moral dilemma and strategic risk
stances.quote: Perhaps the biggest risk-calculation/moral dilemma of the war so far. A massive Russian convoy is abt 30 miles from Kyiv. The US/NATO could likely destroy it. But that would be direct involvement against Russia and risk, everything. Does the West watch in silence as it rolls?

stances.summary: Refutes Putin's false Nazi and genocide claims justifying Ukrainian invasion
stances.quote: Kremlin spokesman says goal of “special operation” in Ukraine: “it is necessary to liberate Ukraine, to clear it of the Nazis.”  But Ukraine is not run by Nazis and Ukrainians say they don’t want Russia to “liberate” them.

stances.summary: Characterizes Putin's genocide claims as propaganda and pretext for war
stances.quote: Smoke and mirrors. Putin just recognized an area in Ukraine he already controls by claiming to be stopping a genocide that isn’t happening.

stances.summary: Disputes Russian separatist claims of Ukrainian military aggression based on field reporting
stances.quote: The separatists are claiming Ukrainians are attacking and besieging them.  I’ve walked up and down those trenches for the last several months.  Saw no signs of ongoing or impending Ukrainian offensive.  None.

stances.summary: Warns against war rhetoric, calls for diplomatic subtlety this administration lacks

stances.summary: Reassures that virus not catastrophic, emphasizes precautions needed
stances.quote: Two virologists I’ve spoken to say coronavirus is not an end of days virus. They say take precautions/work for a vaccine, but emphasized this isn’t “the big one.”

stances.summary: Urges calm, notes danger concentrated among vulnerable populations
stances.quote: Don’t panic. Doctors/ virologists I’m speaking to say 98% of people will be fine, even if they get Covid-19. They expect it will go around the world, but that most people who get it will be a little sick, then recover. The danger is to vulnerable people. Hospitals/ old age homes.

stances.summary: Warns virus more widespread and dangerous than publicly reported
stances.quote: A dr treating coronavirus victims in hong kong just told me he doesn't think the world is aware of the dangers.  Thinks, based on what he’s seen, the virus is far more widespread than being reported.  “If you see one cockroach, you know there are more”

stances.summary: Criticizes Trump's inconsistent Middle East policy and broken ally commitments

stances.summary: Reports international sources believe US has become the bad actors
stances.quote: The more I talk talk to sources, the more i’m hearing America’s betrayal of the Kurds, and the humiliation, “misogynistic” “squashing” of US ambassador in Ukraine for political motivations makes people think, we, Americans, have become the “bad guys.”  Hearing it was gut punch.

stances.summary: Condemns attacks on Kurds, reports US military officials ashamed and sickened

stances.summary: Criticizes Biden's human rights rhetoric as hollow given Afghanistan collapse
stances.quote: Biden says human rights center of US policy. A hard sell tonight where im sitting outside the kabul airport.

stances.summary: Condemns US intelligence failure regarding Taliban peace process deception
stances.quote: More on intel failure. How did the US get duped into thinking there was ever a peace process with the Taliban?  Outfoxed by the Taliban?  I’d say that’s embarrassing but shameful is closer

stances.summary: Criticizes major US intelligence failure in predicting Afghan city collapse
stances.quote: The failure to anticipate the rapid fall of afghan cities, including kabul, is a huge US intelligence failure. I know some US mil commanders anticipated it.  They told me.  Yet somehow their voices were not heard.

stances.summary: Disputes spontaneous protest narrative of January 6 Capitol riot
stances.quote: Remember how John McCain said spontaneous protesters in Benghazi don’t show up with RPGs and mortars?  Spontaneous demonstrators also don’t show up to a protest with IEDs and flex cuffs (designed to restraining detainees)

stances.summary: Implies police coordination or complicity with January 6 protesters
stances.quote: Police seemed very chummy with the protesters who also seemed to know exactly where to go.

stances.summary: Characterizes Capitol riot as coup attempt by international standards
stances.quote: In other nations, when demonstrators, urged by a cornered president, try to take over the capital building it’s called a coup. Nothing else.

stances.summary: Mourns lost opportunities and rights for Afghan women under Taliban return
stances.quote: Thinking tonight about all the Afghans who only knew what life was like over the past 20 years. There was violence, yes, but also hope and opportunities. Now both are gone, especially for girls and women.

stances.summary: Argues Taliban resurgence represents worse outcome than original empowerment
stances.quote: Some say Afghanistan is coming full circle. Taliban were in power, now returning. It’s much worse than that: people tasted freedom, and Taliban can now claim they drove the US out.  So it’s not back to the beginning, but to a new, far worse place.

stances.summary: Criticizes Fox News for false transparency claims about vote counting
stances.quote: Just watched a fox news reporter criticizing a lack of transparency in vote counting while he was INSIDE a voting center, as ballots were calmly being processed behind him.

stances.quote:
The US national archives - the supposed official record and repository of the nation - is now blurring and censoring historic moments? erasing/editing history to appease the powerful or placate the easily offended.  History is what it is.
 https://t.co/oblUuAQMvo

stances.summary: Views military resistance to potential Trump coup as critical democratic guardrail
stances.quote: Seems like some in the military, now openly being encouraged by respected former commanders, have decided they will not takeover America for President Trump. A possible tipping point.  Certainly would have been, had it gone the other way.

stances.summary: Explains Kurds sharing intelligence to document vital ISIS-fighting role
stances.quote: There’s a reason Kurds are sharing so much intelligence. They want to show they played, and still play, a vital role fighting ISIS. That they lost 11,000 people doing it, and should not be abandoned by the US while their homeland is under attack. It's not about bragging rights.

stances.summary: Reports international perception of US mass shootings as preventable, government failure
stances.quote: From abroad, the mass shootings in the US seem like a preventable illness. Two friends in the UK independently told me “if Americans don’t want to fix the problem, I can’t feel sorry for them.”  It gave me pause.

stances.summary: Praises Biden's inaugural speech tone as contrast to Trump's divisiveness
stances.quote: Biden speech. None of the Trump swagger. Not sarcastic. Not all about him. It’s about America. About healing. About respect. About opportunities. This is the kind of speech that attracted people of the world to the United States for many years.
